run.decision: FAIL / VALIDATION_FAIL, COMPARISON_PASS. The frozen one-year post-halving strategy produced 23.948521% CAGR, 0.738844 Sharpe and 37.969088% MDD after conservative product-level costs. Both complete tradeable event windows were positive after entry/exit costs: 2020 401.376348% and 2024 32.978800%. It improves Sharpe and MDD versus BTC buy-and-hold (0.677756, 82.442839%), therefore comparison=PASS. But 37.97% MDD breaches the <=25% intrinsic floor and Sharpe<1, so validation/objective FAIL. Global DSR=0.00472707006; only two complete active halving windows exist. No event-window or technical rescue is permitted.

methodology.follow_up_policy: After formal performance is viewed, do not change the 365-day window, add a pre-halving window, combine technical signals, alter weekend policy, data source or costs. A different supply-cycle hypothesis is a new preregistered lineage, not rescue tuning.
pass_fail_gates: both complete tradeable halving windows have positive net return after entry and exit costs
max realized gross <=100% and minimum cash >=0
methodology.selection_metric: No window search. For each already-observed halving, hold BTC only on execution dates strictly after the halving and no later than halving+365 calendar days. No estimated future halving may trigger exposure. Validation, objective and BTC buy-hold comparison are separate ATM-SVP-3 axes; final validation is capped at WEAK because only two complete tradeable halving windows exist in the frozen sample.

run.title: btc-halving-001 / 比特币减半供给冲击001; deterministic one-year post-halving exposure

strategies.description: Bitcoin halvings mechanically reduce new-coin issuance. If the supply shock is economically meaningful but price adjustment is not instantaneous, holding BTC for one fixed calendar year after each observed halving may concentrate exposure in the post-supply-shock repricing phase while avoiding much of the multi-year crypto bear-cycle exposure between halvings. The rule contains no price indicator and is independent of BTC SMA200-001.

version.mechanism_text: Bitcoin halvings mechanically reduce new-coin issuance. If the supply shock is economically meaningful but price adjustment is not instantaneous, holding BTC for one fixed calendar year after each observed halving may concentrate exposure in the post-supply-shock repricing phase while avoiding much of the multi-year crypto bear-cycle exposure between halvings. The rule contains no price indicator and is independent of BTC SMA200-001.

allowed_changes: use exact frozen Binance BTCUSDT data and SEC halving-date file
treat USDT as USD-equivalent and convert with identical historical usd_per_cny path used in BTC SMA200-001
restrict execution to BTC x SP500 common sessions for metric comparability
halving date itself is unavailable for exposure; enter on the next common execution session
hold 100% BTC through the 365th calendar day after an observed halving, then cash
report both 2020 and 2024 event-window net returns including entry and exit costs
forbidden_changes: using pre-halving windows or estimated future halving dates
combining halving with SMA, momentum, RSI, ATR, MVRV, volume, funding, drawdown or stop-loss rules
adding ETH, QQQ, gold or TLT after results
using weekend execution after seeing common-session results
changing transaction costs or USDT/USD treatment after results
shorting, borrowing, financing, leverage or gross exposure above 100%

shared_rules.enter_rule: first common execution date strictly after halving
shared_rules.exit_rule: first common execution date after halving+365 calendar days
